items.title: Modi, Trump stress keeping Strait of Hormuz open amid Iran war

featured_image.name: Modi, Trump discuss importance of keeping Strait of Hormuz open

items.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump spoke by phone on Tuesday, their first conversation since the United States and Israel launched coordinated strikes against Iran on February 28. The call focused on the escalating conflict in the Middle East and the need to keep the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint for roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply — open and accessible.[1][2]

"Received a call from President Trump and had a useful exchange of views on the situation in West Asia," Modi wrote on X. "India supports de-escalation and restoration of peace at the earliest. Ensuring that the Strait of Hormuz remains open, secure and accessible is essential for the whole world."[3]

U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor confirmed the call, writing on X that the two leaders "discussed the ongoing situation in the Middle East, including the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz open." A White House official confirmed the conversation but declined to comment on its substance.[4][1]

items.title: Aid flotilla docks in Havana as US oil blockade deepens Cuba's crisis

featured_image.name: Aid flotilla arrives in Cuba as US oil blockade worsens energy crisis | The  Independent

items.description:
The first vessel of a humanitarian flotilla carrying medical supplies, food, and solar panels docked in Havana on Tuesday, delivering aid to Cuba as a US fuel blockade deepens the island's energy crisis. The Maguro, a shrimp fishing boat symbolically renamed after Fidel Castro's legendary yacht Granma, arrived three days later than planned after battling strong winds, currents, and mechanical trouble during its voyage from Mexico.[1][2][3]

Two more ships were expected to arrive Tuesday or Wednesday as part of a broader air-and-sea mission dubbed the "Our America Convoy to Cuba," which aims to deliver roughly 50 tonnes of supplies to the island.[2][4]

items.title: Iran toughens negotiation stance, presses US for major concessions

featured_image.name: Iran toughens negotiating stance amid mediation efforts ...

items.description:
Iran's negotiating posture has hardened sharply since the US-Israeli military campaign began last month, with Tehran now demanding guarantees against future military action, compensation for wartime losses, and formal control of the Strait of Hormuz before it will engage in any substantive talks with the United States, according to a Reuters report citing three senior sources in Tehran.[1][2]

The demands, which also include a categorical refusal to discuss any limitations on Iran's ballistic missile program, are likely to be non-starters for President Donald Trump and mark a dramatic shift from the more conciliatory tone Iran struck during earlier rounds of indirect nuclear negotiations.[3][1]

items.description:

items.description:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump spoke by phone on Tuesday, with both leaders stressing the need to keep the Strait of Hormuz open as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran continues to disrupt global energy supplies and rattle economies worldwide.

Trump initiated the call, according to U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, who said on X that the two leaders "discussed the ongoing situation in the Middle East, including the importance of keeping the Strait of Hormuz open". Modi, in his own post on X, said he had a "useful exchange of views" and reiterated India's position. "India supports de-escalation and restoration of peace at the earliest. Ensuring that the Strait of Hormuz remains open, secure and accessible is essential for the whole world," Modi wrote.[1][2][3]

items.title: Altman exits Helion board as OpenAI eyes massive fusion deal

featured_image.name: OpenAI Eyes Fusion Energy Deal With Helion for Future Power Supply | AI  News Hub

items.description:
OpenAI is negotiating a massive power purchase agreement with fusion startup Helion Energy that could deliver 5 gigawatts of electricity by 2030 and scale to 50 gigawatts by 2035, according to a report by Axios on Monday citing a person familiar with the talks. Sam Altman, OpenAI's CEO and Helion's largest individual investor, has stepped down from Helion's board of directors to avoid conflicts of interest as the two companies move toward a partnership.[1][2][3][4]

The proposed deal would give OpenAI a guaranteed 12.5% share of Helion's projected energy output, dwarfing every existing commercial fusion agreement. For context, Helion's only signed power contracts to date are a 50-megawatt deal with Microsoft struck in 2023 and a 500-megawatt plant being developed with steelmaker Nucor — making the OpenAI framework 100 to 1,000 times larger than anything the company has committed to before.[5][3][1]

items.title: 20-year study finds mammal cloning hits genetic dead end after 58 generations

featured_image.name: Starting with one mouse, scientists create 581 successive clones

items.description:
A 20-year experiment in Japan has revealed that mammals cannot be cloned indefinitely, with researchers producing 58 generations of mice from a single donor before the cloned animals accumulated so many genetic mutations they could not survive past their first day of life.

The study, published Tuesday in Nature Communications, was led by geneticist Sayaka Wakayama and developmental biologist Teruhiko Wakayama at the University of Yamanashi. Beginning in 2005, the team used somatic cell nuclear transfer — the same technique that produced Dolly the sheep — to serially clone a single female mouse, producing more than 1,200 offspring across nearly six decades of clonal generations.[1][2]
